messages.content: I'm looking to contribute to the Chinese translation for the FastAPI docs as discussed in issue #1228. Which files in docs/zh/ are currently unassigned and ready for me to pick up?

It's great to have you on board! Currently, docs/zh/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md and docs/zh/advanced/async-sql.md are available. Please check the latest comments in issue #1228 to ensure no one else has claimed them in the last few hours. Once you decide, comment there so we can mark them as in-progress.

Thanks for the update. I'll take on docs/zh/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md. I noticed that some of the existing translations in the docs/zh/ directory are using inconsistent terminology for 'dependency injection'. Should I stick to a specific glossary, or is there a style guide I should follow?

Good catch. We try to maintain consistency by referencing the main English docs style. For 'dependency injection', please use '依赖注入'. If you're unsure about other terms, check the glossary inside the CONTRIBUTING.md file in the root directory. Feel free to open a draft PR when you have the first few sections translated so we can review the terminology.

I've started working on the introduction section of docs/zh/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md. I'm running into some rendering issues when using mkdocs locally. When I run 'mkdocs serve', the custom admonitions in the Chinese files aren't rendering correctly compared to the English ones.

That sounds like a potential configuration mismatch in mkdocs.yml. Check if your local environment has the same 'pymdownx.details' extensions enabled as the main config. Also, verify that your local 'pip install -r requirements-docs.txt' is up to date, as some admonition features require specific versions of 'mkdocs-material'.

You were right, my 'mkdocs-material' version was outdated. After upgrading via 'pip install -U mkdocs-material', the admonitions render perfectly. However, now I'm getting an 'AttributeError: module 'mkdocs' has no attribute 'plugins'' error during build. I'm worried it might be related to the theme settings.

That error often occurs if your 'mkdocs.yml' is referencing a plugin that isn't installed or is incompatible with your current environment. Double-check your site-packages to ensure 'mkdocs-material' and all dependencies listed in 'requirements-docs.txt' are correctly linked. Try deleting your 'site/' folder and running 'mkdocs build --clean' to clear any stale cache.

Cleaning the site directory resolved the build error! I've finished translating the initial sections of 'docs/zh/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md'. I've pushed the changes to my fork and opened a draft PR. Can you take a look at the phrasing for the OAuth2 scope definitions?

I've reviewed your PR. The structure looks solid, but in the section 'Scope 权限定义', consider using '作用域' instead of '权限' for scope, as it's the standard technical term in FastAPI's context. Your translation of the security dependency logic is very clear and accurate compared to the source file.

I've made the suggested change to use '作用域'. I noticed that some of the code snippets in docs/zh/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md have outdated FastAPI version headers. Should I update those to 0.100.0 or keep them consistent with the original file's versioning?

Always keep the code snippets consistent with the original English version to avoid confusion. If the original docs use an older version header, leave it as is for now. We usually track documentation updates and version bumps separately. Your focus should remain on the accuracy of the Chinese translation text itself.

Understood. I've finished the remaining translation for docs/zh/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md. I noticed a typo in the English source file docs/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md (a missing closing backtick in a code block). Should I fix that in the same PR?

Yes, please! If you spot an error in the source file, feel free to include a fix in a separate commit within your PR. It helps improve the overall quality of the FastAPI documentation. Just mention it in the PR description so we can attribute the fix correctly during the merge.

Done! I've added a commit fixing the typo in the English file and finalized the translations in docs/zh/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md. Is there anything else I need to do before the PR can be merged?

Everything looks great. Since this is a translation, I'll perform one final cross-check against the English docs to ensure no sections were skipped. I'll also notify the other team members on issue #1228 that your file is ready for review. You've done excellent work here.
Thanks! I'm happy to help. While waiting for the review, I'd like to pick up another file. Is docs/zh/advanced/async-sql.md still free, or has someone else claimed it since we last spoke?

Let me check the tracking issue #1228... Yes, it's still available! Please go ahead and update the comment on that issue to claim it so we can keep the tracking organized. I'll be here if you run into any more technical hurdles with your local environment setup for that file.

Confirmed, I've updated the issue comment and claimed docs/zh/advanced/async-sql.md. I'll get started on the initial read-through. Are there any specific libraries I should be aware of that might affect technical phrasing for the async SQL content?

For 'async-sql.md', focus on consistent usage of '异步' (asynchronous) and '连接池' (connection pool). Since it covers SQLAlchemy, ensure the translation aligns with their official Chinese documentation terminology if applicable. Good luck with the next file, and thanks for your continued contribution to the community!

I'm deep into docs/zh/advanced/async-sql.md now. I noticed that for the code snippets using 'databases' and 'SQLAlchemy', the terminology for 'session' and 'transaction' is sometimes handled differently. Should I use '会话' for session? And what about '事务' for transaction?

Yes, '会话' for session and '事务' for transaction are the standard terms used across the FastAPI documentation. Using them consistently helps maintain the professional tone. Remember to check if any of these terms appear in the glossaries of existing files like docs/zh/tutorial/sql-databases.md for reference.

Good point. I checked docs/zh/tutorial/sql-databases.md, and it confirms the terminology. However, I've run into a block with the 'async with' syntax translation. How should I translate the phrase 'asynchronous context manager' to flow naturally in Chinese?

You could use '异步上下文管理器' which is the standard technical translation in the Python community. It is a bit verbose, but it's precise. Make sure it fits well in the sentence structure; sometimes rearranging the clause helps readability in Chinese technical documents.

That works perfectly. I've finished the first draft of the translation for docs/zh/advanced/async-sql.md. I am noticing some inconsistencies in the markdown formatting, specifically with how the nested lists are indented compared to the original English files. Does the linter check this?

The project uses markdownlint. You can run 'npm run lint:md' if you have the dependencies installed. If you encounter errors, just ensure the indentation levels match the four-space convention used across the docs/ directory. It keeps the output consistent when rendered.

Running the linter now... it flagged a few warnings about trailing spaces in docs/zh/advanced/async-sql.md. I'll clean those up. Once done, do I need to re-verify the links? Some internal references in the tutorial might have changed since the last sync.

Good catch. Use the 'pytest' suite with '--docs' flag if configured, or just manually verify that the cross-links like '../tutorial/sql-databases.md' still resolve correctly within your local preview. We don't want broken navigation in the generated MkDocs site.

Everything looks solid now. I've successfully linted the file and verified the internal links. One small question: should I add a version notice at the top of the Chinese version if the content is specific to FastAPI 0.100.0?

If the English source doesn't have it, don't add it. We aim for parity. Your changes look great, please go ahead and push your changes to your fork. Let me know the PR number once you open it so I can track it.
Done! I've opened PR #1235 for docs/zh/advanced/async-sql.md. While that's under review, I saw that the 'websockets' section of the docs might be needing some attention. Is that an open target?

I'll take a look at PR #1235 in a moment. For the 'websockets' section, yes, it has been flagged as outdated in the Chinese version. It's a larger task than 'async-sql.md', so be prepared for a bit more work if you want to tackle that.

I'm ready for the challenge. I'll claim docs/zh/tutorial/websockets.md on the issue tracker. Just to be safe, are there specific caveats for WebSocket terminology? I'm thinking about 'handshake' or 'event loop' specifically.

For 'handshake', use '握手'. For 'event loop', use '事件循环'. Those are universally accepted. I've just merged your 'async-sql.md' PR, so your work is now officially part of the documentation. Great job on the quick turnaround!

That's fantastic news! I'm glad to see it merged. I've just started reading through the source for docs/tutorial/websockets.md. It's quite comprehensive. Should I break this translation into smaller commits based on the sub-headings?

That's a smart strategy. Breaking it into logical chunks—like 'Creating a WebSocket', 'Client-side', and 'Handling Events'—makes the review process much easier for us. Please keep that structure in your local git history as you work.

I'll follow that structure. I noticed the WebSocket examples use 'asyncio' quite heavily. Is there anything in the translation guide about documenting 'asyncio' specific patterns versus 'FastAPI' abstractions?

Focus on the FastAPI abstractions first. If you need to mention 'asyncio', keep it minimal. The goal is to show how FastAPI simplifies these patterns. Check the existing translation of docs/zh/tutorial/concurrency.md to see how we handle 'asyncio' concepts there.
I see. I'll align with the concurrency doc styles. I'm starting the translation of the 'Broadcasting' section now. I should be able to finish the first draft by tomorrow.
Sounds perfect. Don't rush; quality is more important than speed. If you have questions about specific WebSocket code behaviors during translation, just ask. Happy translating!

I've hit a slight snag while translating the broadcasting section. In docs/tutorial/websockets.md, there's a reference to an 'asyncio.Queue'. Should I translate the class name itself, or just describe it as an asynchronous queue? I want to make sure developers who look at the code examples don't get confused by the mix of English and Chinese in the documentation text.

Great question. In the FastAPI documentation, we generally keep the class names like 'asyncio.Queue' in English code blocks and references, as that's exactly what the user will see in their IDE. Just describe its function in the text as '异步队列' (asynchronous queue). Keeping technical identifiers consistent is standard practice in our translation guide.

That makes sense. I'll stick to that convention. I've finished the draft for the 'Broadcasting' section and pushed it locally. Should I run the linting script, maybe 'scripts/lint.sh', before I open the PR to ensure I didn't mess up any markdown formatting?

Running 'scripts/lint.sh' is definitely recommended. It catches formatting issues that might break the build or look off in the docs. Also, check the file naming convention in 'docs/zh/tutorial/websockets.md' against the other files in the same directory to make sure the relative paths for images or links are still valid.

The lint script finished, but it flagged an error in 'docs/zh/tutorial/websockets.md'. It seems like I broke a link to 'docs/tutorial/dependencies.md'. I'll fix that. Also, I noticed some internal links in the English docs are absolute. Should I keep those or make them relative in the Chinese version?

Good catch! Please use relative links for all internal references. It prevents breakage if the structure changes or if someone is hosting a localized version under a different base URL. The lint script usually complains if it sees full HTTP paths where it expects relative paths, so that's likely the cause.

I've updated the links to be relative. I'm feeling confident about this section now. Quick question: regarding 'WebSocketMiddleware', is that considered a core FastAPI concept that needs a specific term, or should I leave it as is? I haven't seen a consensus in the glossaries.

Good intuition. Keep 'WebSocketMiddleware' exactly as it is in the English text. It's a specific class name, and translating it could mislead developers looking for it in the codebase. Just add a brief explanation in parentheses like '中间件 (middleware)' if you feel it helps, but don't translate the class name itself.

Understood. Everything is coming together. I've finished the full translation of 'docs/zh/tutorial/websockets.md'. I'm going to run the docs preview build locally. If that looks clean, I'll submit the PR. Any final advice on reviewing the generated HTML?

Excellent. When reviewing the preview, pay close attention to the code blocks. Sometimes long lines get wrapped strangely in the Chinese version due to character width differences. Ensure the 'async' keywords and function signatures are readable on different screen widths.

The preview looks good! I noticed that the code indentation for the broadcasting example looks a bit cramped. I'll adjust the spacing to ensure it reads well. I am preparing the PR now. Should I reference the GitHub issue #1228 in the commit message?

Yes, please do! Adding 'Closes #1228' or just mentioning it in the description helps us keep the tracking issue up to date. It makes it easier for the maintainers to see that your part of the work is complete.

Done! PR submitted for docs/zh/tutorial/websockets.md. It feels good to have that checked off. I've also checked the tracking issue and updated my status. What's the next most pressing area for the Chinese translation project?

Fantastic job! I've tagged the PR for review. Regarding the next steps, 'docs/zh/tutorial/security/index.md' is currently waiting for someone to take it. It's a large one, covering OAuth2 and JWT. Are you feeling up for that, or would you prefer something shorter?

That sounds like a massive undertaking, but I'd like to help. Let me read through 'docs/tutorial/security/index.md' first to gauge the complexity. Is there any particular glossary for 'OAuth2' terminology in Chinese that I should follow?

Security can be tricky. We try to use standard terms like '授权' (authorization) and '认证' (authentication). Check the existing translations in 'docs/zh/tutorial/security/' if any have been started. We want to be consistent with the RFC definitions translated into Chinese.

I'll do some homework on those definitions. I might start by setting up a local test environment for the security tutorials to verify the examples while I translate. Would that be helpful for verifying the content?

That would be incredibly helpful. Actually, if you find any discrepancies between the existing code examples and current FastAPI security patterns, please note them in the PR. Sometimes our docs examples lag behind the latest library updates.
Will do. I'll start by checking the dependencies and the 'security' module imports. I'll reach out if I find any outdated patterns in the tutorial code. Thanks for all the guidance so far!

You are very welcome! You've become a key contributor to this initiative. Take your time with the security section—it's high-visibility and needs to be rock solid. Let me know if you run into any issues with the build pipeline.

I've started auditing 'docs/tutorial/security/first-steps.md'. I noticed that the current example in 'src/security/first-steps.py' uses a slightly outdated approach for 'OAuth2PasswordBearer' instantiation. Should I update the code block in the translated document to the modern pattern?

Great catch! Yes, please update it. We want the Chinese translation to reflect the best practices in the latest FastAPI version. Make sure the import statement 'from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer' remains correct and that the 'tokenUrl' parameter is handled according to our current standards.

Understood. I am modifying the file to ensure the 'tokenUrl' points correctly to the login endpoint. I'll also run a quick test using 'pytest' against the 'tests/test_security_tutorial.py' to ensure my changes don't break the existing CI pipeline logic.

Excellent idea. Running the existing test suite is the best way to catch regressions. If you find any tests failing that aren't related to your translation, please note that in the PR as well; it helps us keep the main repository healthy.

The tests passed locally! Now I'm diving into the actual translation. I'm focusing on 'docs/zh/tutorial/security/first-steps.md'. Translating the conceptual parts of 'OAuth2' is tough—how do you prefer to handle technical acronyms? Should I keep them in English or provide a Chinese equivalent?

Usually, we keep the acronym like 'OAuth2' or 'JWT' in the text for clarity, perhaps adding the Chinese explanation in parentheses the first time it appears. For 'OAuth2PasswordBearer', keep the class name exactly as it is in the code blocks so users can reference it easily.

That makes sense. I'm hitting a slight snag with the term 'scope'. Is '作用域' the preferred translation in our glossary for security scopes, or should I stick to 'scope' to avoid confusion for developers?

Good question. '作用域' is common, but in the context of OAuth2, many developers prefer keeping 'scope' or using '授权范围' (authorization scope). I'd recommend using '授权范围 (scope)' to satisfy both newcomers and experienced developers.

Perfect, that clears it up. I'm making progress on the first section. I've encountered a mention of 'FastAPI's Security utilities'. Should I link that directly to the official API reference or just keep it as a plain text reference?

Always better to use relative links if possible. Check 'docs/zh/reference/security.md' if it exists. If not, linking to the English API docs is acceptable for now to ensure readers have access to the full technical details.

I couldn't find a corresponding Chinese reference for the security utilities yet, so I'll link to the main API reference for now. Moving on to 'get-current-user.md', the logic for 'Depends' seems vital here. Is there any specific formatting for dependencies in our style guide?

Yes, we emphasize that 'Depends' is a central concept. Ensure you use the 'code' format for 'Depends' every time it appears. It's often helpful to bold it for emphasis as it is a core mechanism of FastAPI's dependency injection system.

I've applied that formatting. I am now reviewing the 'get-current-user.md' text for flow. It feels a bit dry. Can I add a brief note about why 'Depends' makes security implementation easier compared to other frameworks?

Absolutely. Adding context on the 'why' behind the design is very valuable for the reader. Just keep it concise so we don't deviate too far from the original structure of the document. The goal is to make the tutorial approachable.

I've drafted the note and integrated it. I'm feeling confident about this section. Do you think it's time for a preliminary review of these two files, or should I complete the whole security sequence first?
I think a preliminary review of 'first-steps.md' and 'get-current-user.md' is a great idea. It lets us check the tone and glossary usage early before you commit to the rest of the security module.
Sounds like a plan. I will push these two files to a new branch 'feature/zh-security-part1' and open a draft PR so you can take a look at the formatting and language usage.

That sounds perfect. Once you open the PR, I'll go through the 'first-steps.md' and 'get-current-user.md' files. I'll look specifically at the terminology we discussed and the link structure you implemented.

PR is up! I've linked it to issue #1228 as we discussed earlier. I'm ready for your feedback whenever you have a moment. I really want to make sure the technical nuances of the security implementation remain precise.
I've just received the notification for the PR. I'll review it today. Your diligence in cross-referencing with the code examples is exactly what we need for a high-quality translation. Talk soon!

I've started reviewing the 'first-steps.md' file again while waiting for your review. I noticed that the term 'OAuth2' is sometimes used as a noun and sometimes as an adjective in my translation. Should I standardize this usage?

Consistency is key. Generally, it's better to use 'OAuth2' as an adjective, like 'OAuth2 specification' or 'OAuth2 flow'. If you're referring to the standard itself, using 'the OAuth2 protocol' or 'the OAuth2 standard' is usually more natural in Chinese technical writing.

That makes sense. I'll update the occurrences in 'first-steps.md' to follow that pattern. Also, in 'get-current-user.md', I found a slight inconsistency in how 'scope' is translated. I am currently using '作用域', is that acceptable for this context?

Yes, '作用域' is the industry standard for 'scope' in the context of authentication and dependency injection in FastAPI. Keep it consistent throughout the entire documentation set to avoid confusing the reader.
Great, I'll stick with '作用域'. I've pushed the updates to 'feature/zh-security-part1'. Are there any specific parts of the PR review you want me to prioritize for the next cycle?

Please prioritize the 'Depends' formatting we discussed. I noticed one instance in the 'get-current-user.md' intro where it might have been missed. Also, check the code blocks for any missing syntax highlighting markers.

Good catch on the 'Depends' marker. I'll audit the file now. Regarding code blocks, I noticed the Python example using 'secrets.compare_digest' needs to be clear. Should I add a comment block for the Chinese explanation?

Adding comments directly into the code blocks is a great way to help beginners. Just ensure the comments don't break the actual execution of the code snippet. Keep them short and placed above the line they explain.
Understood. I will add those comments to 'get-current-user.md' and double-check the 'compare_digest' usage. Is it necessary to add a link to the official Python 'secrets' module documentation?

Yes, linking to the official Python docs is excellent practice, especially for security-related modules. Use a relative link or a standard reference format that matches our existing style guide in the repository.
I've added the link to the Python 'secrets' documentation. The PR is now updated. Should I move on to 'simple-oauth2.md' or wait for your final approval on these two files first?
I think you can safely start working on 'simple-oauth2.md' in a new branch. I am finishing the review of the current PR now and it looks very solid. I'll provide final comments shortly.
That's encouraging! I'll create 'feature/zh-simple-oauth2' and start drafting the content. I'll keep the same 'Depends' and '作用域' terminology rules in mind.
Sounds good. Make sure you cross-reference the concepts from 'first-steps.md' so the translation flows logically. Are you planning to translate the entire OAuth2 sequence this week?
Yes, my goal is to finish 'simple-oauth2.md' and 'jwt-bearer.md' by Friday. I want to make sure the transition between these documents is smooth for the reader.
That is an ambitious goal. Just ensure you don't sacrifice quality for speed. If you get stuck on the terminology for JWT, feel free to reach out to the community in issue #1228.
Will do. Actually, I noticed 'JWT' is often used as-is in Chinese technical documents. Do you prefer 'JWT' or a full translation like 'JSON Web Token'?
Using 'JWT' is standard. You can introduce it as 'JSON Web Token (JWT)' the first time it appears in the text, and then use 'JWT' for the remainder of the file.
Perfect, that's a clear guideline. I will apply that strategy to 'jwt-bearer.md'. I'm starting the drafting process now. Thank you for your continued guidance!
You're very welcome. Your work is really improving the accessibility of FastAPI for Chinese speakers. I'll monitor the repo for your new PR and check back in soon.

I have finished the first draft of 'simple-oauth2.md'. I noticed some phrasing in the FastAPI documentation regarding 'OAuth2PasswordBearer' that feels slightly awkward when translated directly. I am considering using a more descriptive term for the token retrieval process. Should I stick to the literal translation, or can I be slightly more descriptive to improve readability?

In technical documentation like 'simple-oauth2.md', clarity is prioritized over literal translation. If a descriptive term makes the implementation of 'OAuth2PasswordBearer' clearer for the reader, go for it. Just ensure the code blocks and parameter names remain exactly as they are in the original source to avoid confusion when users try to run the examples.

Understood. I will keep the method names and variable identifiers untouched. Moving on, I have run into a small issue with 'jwt-bearer.md'. When translating the section about 'HTTPBearer', the term 'security scheme' has a few possible translations in Chinese. Which one does the team prefer: '安全方案' or '安全机制'?

Great question. '安全方案' is more commonly used in the context of OpenAPI and Swagger specs, which is what FastAPI leverages under the hood via 'fastapi.security'. I recommend using '安全方案' throughout 'jwt-bearer.md' to maintain consistency with the established terminology in the earlier chapters.

That aligns with my research. I'll standardize on '安全方案'. I am about 60% through 'jwt-bearer.md'. Once I finish, I plan to run the 'scripts/docs.py' test command to ensure my formatting doesn't break any of the generated documentation links. Does that sound like a good validation step?

Yes, running 'scripts/docs.py' is a mandatory step before submitting your PR. It checks for broken cross-references and verifies that the file structure matches the expected hierarchy in 'docs/en/docs/'. If you encounter any '404' errors during the build, double-check your relative links in the markdown files.

I will keep an eye out for those. I noticed that 'docs/zh/docs/tutorial/security/oauth2-jwt.md' might need a slight adjustment to match the updated 'jwt-bearer.md'. Should I update the internal links in the other tutorial files as well, or is that outside the scope of my current task?

If you see a direct dependency, feel free to update the internal links. Maintaining consistency across the Chinese translation tree is highly encouraged. Just make sure the changes are isolated in your current branch so we can review them as part of the 'jwt-bearer.md' PR.

I have completed the draft for 'jwt-bearer.md' and successfully ran the tests using 'scripts/docs.py'. Everything looks green! I'm creating the PR now. Should I reference the GitHub issue #1228 directly in the PR description so the team knows I've completed these two chapters?

Definitely. Linking to #1228 helps the maintainers track the progress of the translation project. Use the syntax 'Closes #1228' if you have fully met the requirements, or 'Refs #1228' if you plan to continue with more sections. I will be looking out for your notification to start the review.

The PR is live! I used 'Refs #1228' as I'm interested in tackling 'security-intro.md' next. I've noticed that 'security-intro.md' relies heavily on Pydantic models. Will I need to translate the Pydantic-specific documentation as well, or should I focus strictly on how FastAPI interacts with them?

Focus primarily on the FastAPI-specific implementation. If you find yourself needing to explain Pydantic deeply, it might be better to keep the explanation brief and link back to the official Pydantic docs. This keeps the FastAPI translation focused and maintainable.

That makes sense. Keeping it scoped to FastAPI will keep the documentation cleaner. I'm starting on 'security-intro.md'. The terminology regarding 'dependency injection' is '依赖注入'. Is this the accepted standard, or is there a more idiomatic way to express this in Chinese dev circles?

'依赖注入' is the industry standard for 'dependency injection' in Chinese programming literature. You are safe to use that. For 'Dependency', keep it as '依赖' when referring to 'fastapi.Depends'. It is widely understood and avoids unnecessary complexity.

Thanks for the confirmation. I am making good progress. I've encountered a section where the original documentation mentions specific security best practices. I want to make sure the nuance isn't lost. Should I add a translator's note for these or just translate the technical recommendation directly?

Avoid translator's notes unless it is absolutely necessary for understanding a technical constraint. It's better to translate the recommendation directly and accurately. If you feel a concept needs more context, try to weave it into the sentence structure itself rather than using footnotes or side-notes.

Got it. I'll focus on integrating the context directly. I'm nearing the end of the 'security-intro.md' draft. Once this is done, the core security sections should be covered. Do you think it would be helpful to create a glossary file for common terms at this point?

A glossary would be an excellent contribution to the repository! It would certainly help future contributors maintain consistency. Perhaps you could draft it in a file named 'docs/zh/CONTRIBUTING.md' or 'docs/zh/GLOSSARY.md'. This would be very well received by the maintainers.

I think I will draft a 'GLOSSARY.md'. It will help me keep track of all the decisions we've made so far, like '安全方案' and '依赖注入'. I'll submit this as a separate PR after I finish the current one. Thanks for all your support!
You are doing fantastic work. The 'GLOSSARY.md' idea shows great foresight. I'll be here if you hit any roadblocks during the final review of 'security-intro.md'. Good luck with the final polish!

I've just finished the final pass on security-intro.md. I noticed a slight inconsistency in how I referred to 'OAuth2 scopes' across the document. Should I consistently use 'OAuth2 作用域' or keep it as 'OAuth2 Scopes' for better readability?

Consistency is key in technical documentation. Using 'OAuth2 作用域' is more professional and readable for a Chinese-speaking audience. I recommend updating all instances to that term, and be sure to add '作用域' to your draft in docs/zh/GLOSSARY.md for reference.

Good call. I've updated the draft and pushed the changes to the branch. While re-reading, I noticed some of the examples in security-intro.md use 'HTTPBasic' authentication. Is it standard to translate the class names, or should I leave those in English?

Class names and code identifiers must never be translated. Keep 'HTTPBasic', 'OAuth2PasswordBearer', and other class names from fastapi.security exactly as they appear in the original source. Translating these would break the code snippets if a user tries to copy-paste them.

Understood. I will strictly stick to the original code identifiers. I'm finalizing the PR for security-intro.md now. Should I include a screenshot or test report for the documentation rendering to prove it builds correctly?

Usually, the CI pipeline on the FastAPI repo will handle the rendering checks using MkDocs. You don't need to include screenshots, but it is good practice to run 'mkdocs serve' locally to ensure there are no broken links or syntax errors in the Markdown formatting before pushing.

I ran 'mkdocs serve' locally and everything looks good! I am ready to open the PR. Since I'm submitting multiple files, including the new GLOSSARY.md, should I group them in one PR or keep them separate?

It is generally preferred to keep the content translation separate from the new documentation structure. Open one PR for 'security-intro.md' and a separate one for 'GLOSSARY.md'. This allows the maintainers to review the content and the project structure independently.

That makes sense. PR for 'security-intro.md' is submitted. I'm now drafting the 'GLOSSARY.md' content based on our previous discussions. Does the format of the glossary matter? Should I use a standard table or a list format?

A table format is usually easier to maintain as it grows. Use three columns: 'Term', 'Chinese Translation', and 'Description'. This makes it very easy for future contributors to scan and verify definitions quickly.

I've drafted the table in 'docs/zh/GLOSSARY.md'. I have entries for 'Dependency Injection', 'Scopes', and 'Authentication'. Are there any other terms that you think are crucial to include before I submit this PR?

You should definitely add 'Middleware' (中间件) and 'Request/Response' (请求/响应) as they appear frequently throughout the FastAPI docs. Also, ensure you define 'Endpoint' (端点) as it's a common point of confusion.
Added those to the glossary. It is looking comprehensive now. I'll push this as a second PR. I feel like this really helps finalize my contribution to the translation effort.

You have done a fantastic job navigating the nuances of technical translation. Your contributions will surely be appreciated by the Chinese-speaking FastAPI community. Is there anything else you need before closing out these tasks?
One last check—I see a section in the docs that mentions 'FastAPI features'. Should I translate that as 'FastAPI 特性' or 'FastAPI 功能'? Both seem valid.

In the context of software documentation, '特性' usually refers to the built-in capabilities or 'features' of the framework. '功能' refers more to user-defined functions. Use '特性' for describing FastAPI's own features.
Perfect, that distinction clears up the ambiguity. I've updated the glossary with '特性'. I am ready to submit the second PR now. Thanks again for your constant guidance throughout this process.
